F1_cascadeLayerInversion.status: DONE — token-read-at-source (the audit's recommended option b, the one-path root cause)
F1_cascadeLayerInversion.fix: ProgressDefault.vue reads --progress-track (root) / --progress-fill (indicator) at SOURCE — `bg-[var(--progress-track,var(--secondary))]` + `[background:var(--progress-fill,var(--primary))]`, the exact gradient-variant idiom — and DROPS the bg-secondary/bg-primary utilities. The .glass-progress-rail recipe FEEDS those tokens (--progress-track/--progress-fill from --progress-rail-track/--progress-rail-fill); the --progress-fill set on the rail root inherits to the indicator child. Now the default variant is token-retintable for EVERY consumer (closing the latent 'default is the only un-retintable variant' defect), NOT just the rail.
F1_cascadeLayerInversion.rejectedAlternative: Re-authoring .glass-progress-rail in @layer utilities purely to out-rank bg-primary on source order — papers the symptom, leaves the default variant un-retintable for every OTHER consumer. NOT chosen for colour.
F1_cascadeLayerInversion.evidence: Live render under :root{--progress-rail-fill:rgb(0,200,0)}: indicator computed background-color = rgb(0,200,0) (override WINS; green=200 dominant). Bite-proven: reverting ONLY the ProgressDefault token-read (re-add bg-primary) -> render REDS (green channel 25, override lost) — the render gate catches the cascade-layer class, not a string.

F1b_geometryCascade.status: DONE — DIVERGENCE/EXTENSION (the render gate surfaced it; in the F1 gestalt)
F1b_geometryCascade.discovery: The render readback the upgraded gate now performs surfaced that the cascade inversion ALSO clobbered the GEOMETRY: the recipe's `height: var(--progress-rail-h,3px)` (and zero radius) in @layer components lost to the variant's `h-4`/`rounded-pill` @layer utilities, so the rail painted as a 16px bar (computed height 16px), NOT the hairline the slice's own close criterion demands ('a hairline sliver, NOT a 16px bar'). The string-scan never saw this; the original AW.W16 recipe shipped a 16px rail GREEN.
F1b_geometryCascade.fix: Re-authored .glass-progress-rail as a Tailwind `@utility glass-progress-rail` (lands in @layer utilities — the idiomatic restyle-class idiom, cf. btn-audacious/cartoon-surface). The hairline geometry is scoped under a doubled-class self-reference (`&&` -> .glass-progress-rail.glass-progress-rail, specificity 0,2,0) so it out-ranks the base h-4/rounded-pill DETERMINISTICALLY regardless of Tailwind's utility emit order — no !important. NOTE this is NOT the rejected colour layer-juggle: colour stays the token-read-at-source path; the @utility only wins the geometry, which has no token-read-at-source alternative (the base Progress legitimately wants h-4; the rail is a restyle).
F1b_geometryCascade.evidence: Live render: rail computed height = 3px (the hairline); the bare single-class @utility tied h-4 and lost (16px) — the `&&` doubled-class fixed it.

F2_clippedGlow.status: DONE — trailing INSET edge inside the clip
F2_clippedGlow.ratifiedForm: The audit's recommended `linear-gradient` right-edge brightening was REJECTED at impl after a runtime check: the indicator carries the @layer-utilities `[background:var(--progress-fill,...)]` SHORTHAND, which resets `background-image` to none and ALWAYS outranks the @layer-components/@utility recipe's `background-image` longhand — so a gradient-image glow would be a silent no-op (the exact same cascade-layer trap as F1, on a different property). The INSET box-shadow fallback the slice names is the correct one-path form: `box-shadow` is a separate property the `[background:...]` shorthand does NOT touch.
F2_clippedGlow.fix: `.glass-progress-rail && > * { box-shadow: inset calc(-1*var(--progress-rail-glow-x,4px)) 0 var(--progress-rail-glow-blur,8px) calc(-1*var(--progress-rail-glow-spread,2px)) color-mix(in srgb, hsl(0 0% 100%) var(--progress-rail-glow-strength,55%), transparent) }` — an inset shadow offset LEFTWARD brightens just inside the indicator's right (leading) edge: a moving position head that never crosses the fill boundary, so the load-bearing overflow-hidden clip cannot eat it (the clip is never lifted).
F2_clippedGlow.evidence: Live render: indicator computed box-shadow = 'color(srgb 1 1 1 / 0.55) -4px 0px 8px -2px inset' (the inset glow renders). Holds light AND dark.
